Basis for Intervening:
Pursuant to Rules 212 and 214 of the Rules of Practice and Procedure of the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission ("Commission"), 18 C.F.R. §§ 385.212 and 385.214, the Data Center Coalition ("DCC") hereby moves to intervene in this proceeding. DCC is the membership organization for the U.S. data center industry, representing leading data center owners and operators that maintain data center infrastructure and teams across the country. DCC members operate data centers that constitute significant loads within the ISO-NE region.

DCC's member companies provide the essential digital infrastructure that underpins the modern economy and supports critical public services, including cloud computing, artificial intelligence, emergency response systems, and public safety operations. From 2017 to 2023, the data center industry contributed $3.5 trillion to U.S. GDP. As the industry unlocks unprecedented economic opportunities across the country and the ISO-NE region, supporting affordability and reliability is a foundational priority for DCC members and the communities they serve. DCC advocates for grid reforms that minimize unnecessary cost burdens, align with cost causation, facilitate responsible load growth, and support the development of new generation without imposing undue costs on existing ratepayers.

DCC members will be directly and substantially impacted by the outcome of this proceeding. DCC has a substantial interest in this proceeding, and no other party can adequately represent the substantial interests of DCC or its diverse and broad set of members. Accordingly, DCC respectfully requests that the Commission grant its timely motion to intervene in this proceeding.
